rationale: Direct neuroimaging and clinical phenotyping from multiple independent cohorts confirm that biallelic loss-of-function (LoF) variants in NOTCH3 produce a distinct clinical and neuroradiological entity (OMIM #621295) that differs markedly from dominant CADASIL. Specifically, systematic neuroradiological analysis of 26 patients with biallelic LoF variants confirmed periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia (PVL) with sparing of the anterior temporal poles, accompanied by cerebral microcalcifications, microbleeds, and basal ganglia lacunes, whereas cysteine-altering variants (both monoallelic CADASIL and biallelic cysteine missense variants) demonstrate deep white matter hyperintensities characteristically affecting the anterior temporal poles without periventricular/periatrial volume loss.

evidence.text: Systematic neuroradiological analysis of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants demonstrated that biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome characterized by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) cause deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss matching the CADASIL spectrum.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: Three patients from two unrelated families harboring biallelic cysteine-sparing loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants demonstrated extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, cerebral atrophy, basal ganglia lacunes, microbleeds, and microcalcifications, with explicit sparing of the anterior temporal lobes, highlighting a phenotype distinct from CADASIL.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared. Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

evidence.text: Evaluation of an individual harboring a homozygous null NOTCH3 variant (c.2984delC) confirmed early-onset leukoencephalopathy with diffuse white matter hyperintensities that specifically lacked anterior temporal pole lesions, providing further evidence of autosomal recessive loss-of-function inheritance distinct from dominant CADASIL.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: WES was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions... identified a novel homozygous NOTCH3 null variant (c.2984delC).

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of periatrial white matter volume loss combined with microcalcifications in differentiating biallelic NOTCH3 LoF from congenital cytomegalovirus and ABCC9-related intellectual disability and myopathy syndrome?
new_directions.rationale: ABCC9 loss-of-function variants and congenital viral infections also present with periventricular leukomalacia and cerebral calcifications; defining precise diagnostic discrimination thresholds between these mimics is necessary.

new_directions.question_text: Does the developmental timing of microcalcification appearance correlate with the onset of childhood ischemic strokes in biallelic NOTCH3 LoF patients?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether vascular calcification precedes or follows ischemic events can clarify whether microcalcification reflects primary arteriopathy calcification or secondary dystrophic parenchymal damage.
